entries.definition: applying a retrieval model to a task/domain for which it received no training data
synonyms_forbidden: out-of-distribution retrieval (use OOD once defined as the abbreviation)

entries.definition: a classical bag-of-words scoring function that ranks documents by weighted term overlap with the query, with no learned parameters
the failure of bag-of-words matching to find relevant documents that share no vocabulary with the query

entries.term: lexical / sparse / dense / late-interaction / re-ranking (architecture families)
entries.definition: lexical: token-overlap scoring; sparse: learned term weights/expansions layered on lexical matching; dense: single-vector embedding similarity; late-interaction: multiple token-level vectors compared at query time; re-ranking: a cross-attention model re-scores a first-stage candidate list
Normalised Discounted Cumulative Gain at rank 10: a graded, rank-position-aware retrieval metric that credits relevant documents more when they rank higher among the top 10 results
building a retrieval test collection's relevance judgements only from the top candidates some existing system(s) returned; everything else is assumed irrelevant
bi-encoder: query and document are embedded independently, then compared; cross-encoder: query and document are encoded jointly with full cross-attention between them

training examples of non-relevant documents chosen either because they are difficult to distinguish from relevant ones (hard negatives) or because they are simply the other examples in the same training batch (in-batch negatives)
appending model-generated queries or terms to a document before lexical indexing, so a later lexical search can match vocabulary the original document lacked
the fraction of a system's top-k retrieved documents that were never judged by annotators

ordering_check: every term's defined_at slot precedes (or equals, for the slot that introduces it) its first_used_at slot, and precedes every later reuse, per plan/paper_architecture.md's row order.
